title: Cisco ACI Upgrade Automation with Claude
tagline: Plan, validate and execute ACI fabric upgrades the Cisco way, with Claude drafting and code executing
audience: Enterprise network operations, data centre, NOC and network automation engineers who run Cisco ACI fabrics, in India and worldwide
prerequisites: Working knowledge of Cisco ACI: APIC, leaf and spine, tenants, vPC
Basic Python and REST API calls with JSON
Familiarity with change management and maintenance windows
Familiarity with an AI coding assistant is helpful, not required
outcomes: Describe the Cisco-recommended ACI upgrade sequence: release selection, pre-upgrade validation, APIC cluster first, then switch groups, then post-checks
Build a Python client for the APIC REST API that discovers the fabric, runs the pre-upgrade validator and returns typed JSON
Use Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK and an MCP server to plan upgrade groups and maintenance windows as schema-validated structured output
Create firmware and maintenance policies with deterministic Python and Ansible only after a human approves the plan in a GitHub pull request and a ServiceNow change
Produce pre and post upgrade evidence, a comparison report, a pause or rollback decision and a complete audit trail

modules.title: The Cisco ACI upgrade process and where upgrades go wrong
topics: Cisco's recommended sequence: target release and release notes, compatibility matrix, pre-upgrade validation, APIC cluster, switch upgrade groups, post-checks
Why vPC peers never share a group, why the cluster must be fully fit, and what bootflash space, faults and NTP drift do to an upgrade
Firmware repository, maintenance policies, maintenance groups and the scheduler as APIC objects
The teaching pattern: Claude plans and explains, deterministic code executes, a human approves, everything is logged
modules.lab: Walk the lab fabric in the APIC GUI and API Inspector, map each Cisco process step to the APIC objects it touches, and write the workflow brief.

modules.title: Claude Code, Agent SDK and MCP setup for the ACI workflow
topics: Installing Claude Code and the Claude Agent SDK in the project repository with a CLAUDE.md that encodes the upgrade rules
Building an MCP server that exposes read-only APIC queries (nodes, firmware, faults, health) as tools
Tool use with structured JSON outputs: defining the inventory and plan schemas Claude must return
Separating read tools from write actions so the agent can observe but never trigger
modules.lab: Stand up the MCP server against the lab APIC and have Claude Code answer fabric questions using only the exposed tools.
modules.deliverable: Working Claude Code and MCP environment.

modules.title: Fabric discovery through the APIC REST API
topics: POST to aaaLogin, token refresh via aaaRefresh, and class and filter queries against fabricNode, topSystem, infraWiNode and firmwareCtrlrRunning
Typed inventory record: node id, role, model, running version, vPC peer, health score, cluster state
Pydantic validation, unit tests with pytest, and rejected-row reporting for incomplete nodes
modules.lab: Implement the discovery client and tests with Claude Code, inspect every diff, and produce inventory.json for the lab fabric.

modules.title: Pre-upgrade validation and explained failures
topics: Running the APIC pre-upgrade validator and the Cisco aci-preupgrade-validation-script and parsing their results
Checking faults, bootflash space, cluster health, NTP, CIMC and configuration backups against the target release
Claude explains each failed check in plain language, cites the query that produced it and marks unknowns
modules.lab: Fill a leaf's bootflash on purpose on the lab fabric, run validation, and have Claude explain the failure and the Cisco-recommended remediation.

modules.title: Upgrade planning with structured outputs
topics: Claude proposes upgrade groups from the inventory: APIC cluster first, vPC peers split, spines balanced, leaves balanced
Mapping groups to maintenance windows and scheduler times in the fabric's local time zone
JSON Schema validation of the plan and automatic rejection of plans that break a rule
Testing the planner with awkward fabrics: odd vPC pairs, mixed models, a degraded APIC
modules.lab: Generate the plan for the lab fabric, feed it a fabric with an unpaired vPC leaf, and prove the schema gate rejects the bad plan.

modules.title: Firmware staging, backups and the change request
topics: Uploading firmware to the APIC repository with firmwareFirmware and firmwareOSource and verifying checksums
Configuration export and snapshot with configExportP and configSnapshot before any change
Creating the ServiceNow change request through the Table API with the plan, windows and risk text drafted by Claude
Tracking approval state with Flow Designer and blocking execution until the change is approved
modules.lab: Stage the target image, take the snapshot, and raise the lab ServiceNow change from the plan with one command.
modules.deliverable: Staged firmware, snapshot and change request.

modules.title: Guardrails, approvals and audit for fabric upgrades
topics: The agent reads; code writes. Maintenance and firmware policies are created only by deterministic Python or Ansible cisco.aci modules
Plan review and approval in a GitHub pull request with GitHub Actions running the validator and schema checks
Window enforcement: no trigger outside the approved schedule, no next group while the last one is unhealthy
Audit log of prompts, tool calls, API calls, approvals and outcomes in a format the change board can read
modules.lab: Open the plan as a pull request, try to apply it before approval and watch the gate refuse, then approve and apply to the lab.

modules.title: Executing the APIC cluster and switch group upgrades
topics: Upgrading the APIC cluster first and polling infraWiNode and firmwareCtrlrFwStatusCont until the cluster is fully fit
Creating maintenance policies and groups per the plan and triggering each group only inside its window
Polling firmwareRunning and maintUpgJob per node, with timeouts, retries and a pause when a node does not return
Claude drafts the status update for the on-call engineer when the runner pauses
modules.lab: Run the APIC cluster upgrade and group A on the physical lab fabric, then replay a recorded node-not-returning response from a mocked APIC and watch the runner pause.

modules.title: Post-upgrade verification, reporting and rollback decisions
topics: Pre and post snapshots of versions, faults, endpoint counts, routes, vPC and interface state compared by code
Claude turns the diff into a readable report with a go, hold or roll back recommendation
Rollback and downgrade options as Cisco documents them, and when to stop the next group
Lessons captured into the runbook for the next fabric
modules.lab: Compare pre and post state for group A, generate the report, and make the go or hold call for group B as a team.

modules.title: Capstone: end-to-end ACI fabric upgrade with evidence bundle
topics: Inventory in, upgraded fabric out: discovery, validation, plan, change, approval, execution, verification
Evidence bundle with validator output, plan, approvals, API log and post-check report
Demo and limitations statement
modules.deliverable: End-to-end upgrade workflow and evidence bundle.

capstone: A repeatable workflow that discovers a Cisco ACI fabric, runs the pre-upgrade validator, has Claude propose a schema-validated upgrade plan, raises and tracks the ServiceNow change, executes the APIC cluster and switch groups through deterministic code only after human approval, and ships a post-upgrade report with a full audit trail.

narration: hook
An A C I fabric upgrade is a weekend you do not get back. Two hundred switches, a cluster that must be fully fit before anything moves, and one bad group away from rebooting both v P C peers.
hook

What if Claude read the validator output, drafted the upgrade plan and explained every step, while deterministic code did the work and a person approved every window? That is A C I upgrade automation, done the Cisco way.
intro
Gennoor Tech presents Cisco ACI Upgrade Automation with Claude.
story

One fabric in. One upgraded fabric out, with every Cisco recommended check completed and recorded. You build the workflow in ten hands-on modules, and each one is something you can run against the lab fabric, review and demonstrate. Claude plans, drafts and explains. Python and Ansible execute. A human approves the consequential actions. Everything is logged.
path0

You start with the process itself, as Cisco documents it. Target release selection, the release notes and compatibility matrix, A P I C cluster first, then switch groups, and why a v P C pair must never sit in the same group. Then you set up Claude Code, the Claude Agent S D K and an M C P server that exposes read-only A P I C queries as tools.
path0

Then discovery. A Python client for the A P I C R E S T A P I that logs in, pulls every node, controller, firmware version, cluster state and health score, and returns typed J S O N. You run the Cisco pre-upgrade validator and the open-source validation script, parse the results, and let Claude explain each failure in plain language, citing the exact query that produced it.
path1

On day two the plan takes shape. Claude proposes upgrade groups from the inventory, keeps v P C peers apart, orders the A P I C cluster before the leaves and spines, and maps every group to a maintenance window. The output is structured J S O N, validated against a schema, so a bad plan is rejected before anyone reads it. You then stage firmware in the repository, take a configuration export and snapshot, and raise the change request in ServiceNow through the Table A P I.
path2

Guardrails come next, and they are specific to this workflow. The agent can read the fabric, but it cannot trigger an upgrade. Every maintenance policy and firmware group is created by deterministic code, after a person approves the plan in a GitHub pull request. Scheduled start times are checked against the approved window, an incomplete validator run blocks the next step, and every decision, prompt and A P I call is written to an audit log you can hand to the change board.
path3

Day three is execution. The runner upgrades the A P I C cluster, waits for the cluster to be fully fit, then moves through the switch groups one at a time, polling firmware status and never starting the next group until the last one is healthy. If a node does not come back, the run pauses and Claude writes the status update for the on-call engineer.
path3

Then verification. Pre and post snapshots of versions, faults, endpoint counts, routes and v P C state are compared by code, and Claude turns the diff into a readable report with a clear go, hold or roll back recommendation that a person signs off.
labs

Execution labs run on a small physical lab fabric with fictional hostnames, three A P I Cs, four leaves and two spines, so the cluster and switch groups really upgrade and reboot. The runner's failure paths are exercised against a mocked A P I C with recorded responses. You will fail a validator check on purpose, watch the pipeline block, fix the fault, and finish an end to end upgrade with the full evidence bundle.
stats
Ten hands-on modules. Three days. Six physical switches upgraded for real in the lab. And zero upgrades triggered without human approval.
who

This course is for enterprise network operations, data centre and automation engineers in India and worldwide who run Cisco A C I fabrics. You need working A C I knowledge, basic Python, and familiarity with R E S T A P I calls. Experience with an A I coding assistant helps but is not required.
